title: Vitamin D Deficiency Increases Mortality Risk in the UK Biobank: A Nonlinear Mendelian Randomization Study
authors: Sutherland JP, Zhou A, Hyppönen E
population: Unrelated UK Biobank participants of White European ancestry aged 37 to 73 years at recruitment (2006 to 2010) with 25-hydroxyvitamin D and genetic data
funder: Primary funding source of the published structured abstract: National Health and Medical Research Council. MEDLINE lists Medical Research Council (UK) grants MC_PC_17228 and MC_QA137853. The full text was not accessible (HTTP 403 at the publisher); the role of the funder was not read.
result: Nonlinear Mendelian randomisation with 35 variants: 18,700 deaths. The association of genetically predicted 25-hydroxyvitamin D with all-cause mortality was L-shaped, with risk falling steeply up to 50 nmol/L; the odds of death were estimated 25% higher at a measured 25-hydroxyvitamin D of 25 nmol/L than at 50 nmol/L (OR 1.25, 95% CI 1.16 to 1.35). The authors state that a genetic approach gives proof of principle and that the strength of the association is approximate.
